tasks.title: Today: connector runs terminate on nothing
tasks.authority_impact: none; presentation-only
acceptance_criteria: Every connector run ends on its own event row, verified by measuring both endpoints
No connector is left drawn against empty space when a day has no event
Lead: renderConnectors re-anchors runs after the rows are replaced (dial.js update())
tasks.notes: Owner-reported: 'the connecting lines also run straight down connecting to nothing, several lines.'

evidence.investigation: 2026-09-17, read-only, no code change. Every connector run was measured end-to-end against the DOM at three governed viewports (420x912, 390x844) using tmp/probe_connectors.py. The run's end lands on its own row at the row's exact vertical centre in every case: at 420px the three runs end at y=235.0/349.8/464.6 against row centres 235.0/349.8/464.5, each 4.0px left of its row's left edge. No run was drawn against empty space, and no run was drawn for an event with no row. The existing browser guard test_connector_runs_start_on_the_dial_and_end_at_their_own_row passes.
evidence.not_reproduced: The reported symptom does not reproduce on the synthetic fixture at any governed mobile width, so this is NOT closed and NOT reclassified: the owner saw it on a device. Two candidate causes remain untested and both need the owner's data. (a) A longer event list than the fixture's three: the events column is internally scrollable (max-height: calc(100vw - 90px)), so a row whose centre falls below the visible scroll viewport would have its run end outside the painted rail. (b) A stale cached JS bundle on the device, which OS-037 already flags as a trap for the same workspace.
evidence.how_to_reproduce: The fixture is scripts/preview_observatory_dial.py with exactly three upcoming events. A repro needs the owner's real event count and the device screenshot, or the fixture extended past the rail's scroll height with the run endpoints re-measured.
evidence.limits: Unchanged behaviour. No route, data, financial or authority change.
evidence.resolution_2026_09_18: REPRODUCED and fixed. The missing condition was the one recorded as untested: a longer event list. The rail (`.obs-dial-events`) is internally scrollable (`max-height: calc(100vw - 102px)`), so with a 14-event horizon the rail's content is 1591px tall inside a 330px client box. Before the fix all 14 rows got a run, and 11 of those rows sat below the rail's visible box; their runs left the dial, ran down past the rail to y=1754, and were cut off by the connector layer's own `overflow: hidden` at y=746.9 -- dashed lines ending in mid-air, which is exactly the owner's 'running straight down connecting to nothing, several lines'. Fixed in two parts: a run is only drawn when its row's centre is inside the rail's visible box, and the rail re-runs renderConnectors on scroll so the surviving runs follow their rows. After the fix the same page draws 3 runs, each ending exactly on its own visible row (0 anomalies), and scrolling the rail to the middle and the bottom re-anchors to ev-7/8/9 and ev-11/12/13 with every run still on a visible row.
evidence.tests_added: tests/meridian/test_dial_js.py::test_dial_connector_runs_never_target_a_row_the_rail_does_not_show (source guard) and tests/browser/test_dial_fidelity.py::test_connector_runs_do_not_target_rows_the_scrolled_rail_does_not_show (behavioural guard over a 14-event horizon at three rail scroll positions). The behavioural guard was verified to FAIL without the fix ('runs are being drawn for hidden rows', 14 runs for 11 hidden rows), so it genuinely catches the regression rather than describing it.
